resourceName: Xuzhou Yanqun MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Power Project
description:
Xuzhou Yanqun MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Power Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Dapeng Town, Tongshan District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Xuzhou Baichang Environmental Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Xuzhou Yanqun MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Yanqun landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
Yanqun landfill site is located in Dapeng Town, Tongshan District, Xuzhou City, and started operation in 2006 with a total design effective capacity of 6,300,000 m3 and a municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 1,000 tons/d and an operational lifespan of 19 years. The project has a total designed capacity 3.201MW (3*1,067kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project started construction on 07/12/2019 and started operation on 24/10/2020. The operation period of the project will end on 31/12/2030.
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Yanqun landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. 
Scenario existing prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity (the same as baseline scenario) 
•	LFG from Yanqun landfill site is released into the atmosphere.
•	Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the ECPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants.   
Project scenario
•	LFG from Yanqun landfill site is partially used for electricity generation. 
•	3×1,067 kW LFG-generator sets  supply electricity to the ECPG.	
The total power generation during the operation period is estimated to be 208,588 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 101,798 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the ECPG.
